presentation.title: Teller Intervention During a Large Cash Withdrawal
presentation.summary: Practice responding when a caller directs a confidential cash withdrawal, supplies a cover story, attacks the teller's questions, and arranges a courier pickup.
presentation.practiceGoal: Tell bank staff the full truth, accept a respectful protective pause, and refuse any caller-directed cash handoff.

stages.stage: Isolation on the way to the bank

warningSigns.sign: An unexpected caller connected a bank account to a criminal investigation and demanded a large cash withdrawal.
The caller ordered secrecy, stayed on the phone, and supplied a home-repair cover story.
The caller attacked respectful teller questions and suggested another branch, an ATM, or a smaller withdrawal.
A supposed bonded courier and confirmation phrase were used to make a cash pickup sound official.
The caller promised that cash would be inspected and returned later.

finalReview.safestAction: End the call and tell a real bank employee the complete story, including any instruction to lie, hide the phone, visit another branch, or give cash to a courier.

realWorldActions.action: A legitimate bank or government agency does not protect an account by asking a customer to withdraw cash for inspection.
Teller questions, a private conversation, a fraud-team review, or a trusted-contact suggestion can be protective support rather than an accusation.
Do not let the caller supply a cover story or keep the call active during a bank conversation.
If cash was withdrawn but not handed over, secure it and tell the bank exactly what happened.
If cash was handed over, stop further contact, preserve call and courier details, contact the real bank promptly, and seek trusted support. Recovery is not guaranteed.

The learner tells the bank exactly what happened, preserves phone and courier details, reviews any account exposure, and uses legitimate reporting channels. The learner is not blamed. Prompt action may help document the loss and prevent more harm, but recovery is not guaranteed.

outcome.label: Cash handed over; recovery started
outcome.heading: You took the strongest next steps after the loss
outcome.explanation: The scammer created the deception. Complete reporting and trusted support can still protect what remains.

warningSigns.sign: The caller stopped responding after the handoff.

artifact.heading: The cash loss is only partly explained
artifact.message: The withdrawal is reported, but the caller's coaching and courier are not disclosed.
artifact.transcript: The simulated cash loss has occurred. Because the bank receives only the cover story, it cannot fully document the exploitation or review related account risk. The learner can still tell the complete story, preserve evidence, and seek trusted support without blame.

outcome.label: Cash handed over; report incomplete
outcome.heading: Important recovery information remains hidden
outcome.explanation: The caller's secrecy should not control the recovery response.

warningSigns.sign: The home-repair story continues after the courier loss.

artifact.heading: The caller offers false recovery
artifact.message: Chris responds with another promise or fee, creating risk of repeat theft after the cash loss.
artifact.transcript: The simulated cash loss has occurred, and the learner continues contacting the fictional caller. Any promised refund, fee, or second procedure remains controlled by the scammer. The learner should stop contact and use independently located bank, reporting, and trusted-support channels. Recovery is not guaranteed.

outcome.label: Cash handed over; repeat theft risk
outcome.heading: The original caller cannot verify a recovery path
outcome.explanation: Stop further contact before another payment or disclosure occurs.

warningSigns.sign: The person who arranged the courier now offers the remedy.

command.displayText: An unexpected caller says $15,000 must be withdrawn for a confidential investigation.

option.text: End the call and contact the real bank
Ask for a case number and more details
Agree to withdraw the cash immediately

command.displayText: The caller supplies a case number, demands secrecy, and provides a home-repair cover story.

option.text: Pause and tell someone trusted the full story
Mute the caller while deciding
Follow the secrecy instructions

command.displayText: The caller orders the learner to keep the phone hidden and use a home-repair story.

option.text: Stop and tell someone trusted
Mute the caller before speaking with the teller
Keep the call hidden and use the cover story

command.displayText: The teller respectfully asks why the cash withdrawal is unusual and whether anyone is directing it.

option.text: Explain the call and instruction to lie
Say it is personal but accept a pause
Say the cash is for home repairs

command.displayText: The teller notices hesitation and offers a private conversation without the caller.

option.text: Abandon the cover story and tell the truth
Keep the reason private but accept the pause
Repeat the home-repair story

command.displayText: The teller and real fraud team disprove the cash-inspection story and offer a trusted-contact call.

option.text: Accept the fraud review and trusted-contact call
Accept the private review but decline a trusted contact
Leave and follow the caller's next instruction

command.displayText: The teller offers privacy, a real fraud-team review, and a trusted contact while the caller remains undisclosed.

option.text: Tell the full story and accept verification
Speak privately but keep the caller secret
Leave and try another branch

command.displayText: The caller attacks the teller and suggests another branch, an ATM, or a smaller withdrawal.

option.text: Return to the teller and explain the attack
Withdraw a smaller amount as a test
Use another branch or ATM

command.displayText: After a smaller withdrawal, the caller arranges a supposed bonded courier with a confirmation phrase.

option.text: Cancel the pickup and secure the cash
Ask to meet the courier in public
Allow the courier to come to the home

command.displayText: The caller arranges a supposed courier to inspect and later return the withdrawn cash.

option.text: Cancel the pickup and contact the bank
Move the meeting to a public place
Allow the home pickup

command.displayText: A courier repeats the caller's confirmation phrase while the caller pressures the learner to hand over cash.

option.text: Do not hand over the cash
Delay while calling someone trusted
Give the courier the cash

command.displayText: The learner retains the cash and chooses how fully to involve the real bank.

option.text: Secure the cash and tell the bank everything
Redeposit the cash but avoid discussing the scam
Keep communicating with Chris for a refund or explanation

command.displayText: The courier left with the cash, and the learner chooses how to begin recovery.

option.text: Tell the bank exactly what happened
Report the withdrawal but not the caller or courier
Keep contacting Chris to demand the cash back

command.displayText: Independent bank contact disproved the cash-inspection story before any withdrawal.
A trusted person helped break the caller's isolation before cash changed hands.
The teller's private pause and real fraud review prevented the withdrawal.
The learner returned to the real teller, and the funds remained protected.
Cash was withdrawn but not handed over, and the real bank began recovery.
The cash was retained, secured, and fully reported to the real bank.
The cash was protected, but the bank received an incomplete account of the scam.
The cash remained with the learner, but continued caller contact created repeat risk.
The courier took the cash; prompt, complete reporting and recovery began.
The courier took the cash, and incomplete reporting limited the bank's response.
The courier took the cash, and continued caller contact created repeat-theft risk.
